caseStudy.label: Hero Banner
caseStudy.text: Opens on "The All Black and Ivory Drop" — a tight two-colorway hero rather than the full range. A focused palette reads as a considered edit, not a clearance rack.

caseStudy.label: Featured Collection
caseStudy.text: Only the Essentials pieces appear here, so there's exactly one decision to make: black or ivory. Narrowing the choice increases the odds of a click.

caseStudy.label: Editorial Section
caseStudy.text: Black and ivory are the two colors every capsule wardrobe leans on, so this section positions Essentials as the foundation pieces you build every other look around.

caseStudy.label: CTA
caseStudy.text: A plain, high-contrast button. After the two-color story is told, the ask should be the simplest moment in the email, not another decision.

caseStudy.label: Hero Banner
caseStudy.text: A single named suit gets the hero spot rather than a collection. Naming one piece ("Stella") gives it a personality, the way a heritage brand names a bag or a shade of lipstick.

caseStudy.label: Featured Collection
caseStudy.text: One suit, likely shown in multiple colorways or on different bodies, so discovery here is about finding your version of Stella rather than browsing many different styles.

caseStudy.label: Editorial Section
caseStudy.text: A hero-piece format signals confidence — it says this suit is strong enough to carry an entire send, which supports a premium read.

caseStudy.label: CTA
caseStudy.text: Simple and direct, pointing straight at the one product just introduced.

caseStudy.label: Hero Banner
caseStudy.text: Leads with "Juntas o por separado, siempre funcionan" (together or apart, they always work) — the hero copy does double duty as the value proposition.

caseStudy.label: Featured Collection
caseStudy.text: Sets are shown styled together and as standalone pieces, so the same product page serves two different shoppers: the set-buyer and the mix-and-matcher.

caseStudy.label: Editorial Section
caseStudy.text: Coordinated styling here is what makes "they always work" credible — it's proof, not just a claim, that the pieces genuinely pair well.

caseStudy.label: CTA
caseStudy.text: One clear button, kept deliberately simple so it doesn't compete with the styling story just told.

caseStudy.label: Hero Banner
caseStudy.text: Dresses extend the brand beyond swim, opening on lifestyle imagery to signal this is a resort wardrobe moment, not just a swimwear restock.

caseStudy.label: Featured Collection
caseStudy.text: Showing dresses builds toward the "resort capsule" idea — swim plus cover-up plus dress — encouraging a bigger basket than a single-category send would.

caseStudy.label: Editorial Section
caseStudy.text: This is where the cross-category story gets sold: dresses styled alongside swim and accessories, not shown in isolation.

caseStudy.label: CTA
caseStudy.text: A simple button that doesn't pick a single product for you — appropriate when the section's job was to sell a lifestyle, not one item.
